Q: command failed and signal SIGKILL on npm install that involves any sh commands A:

It would help to see at least some of the exact error messages that you are getting, they are intended to tell you what is going wrong. It would also help to document what shell commands npm is trying to execute.

Some of the most likely causes, given that you have been changing the machine configuration include:

  1. You may have changed the default shell to one that does not support the commands that npm is trying to execute.
  2. You may have removed permissions that are needed by npm.
  3. You may have rearranged where things are stored, especially the shell itself, and npm can't find what it is looking for.
  4. You may have set the default encoding in the shell to one that is not compatible.
  5. You may have upgraded the system python - this has been known to cause all sorts of strange issues.

Q: How can I set Python 3.5.2 as default Python version on CentOS? A:

Using alternatives to set the default to Python 3.6 still breaks YUM. To fix it, change the python interpreter to /usr/bin/python2.7 in two files. As root:

cat /usr/bin/yum
cat /usr/libexec/urlgrabber-ext-down

Output:

#!/usr/bin/python2.7
#!/usr/bin/python2.7

I found the following article to be useful: How to install Python 3 on CentOS 7.7 using yum/source and set as the default

Q: How to check if a date is after today java A:

tl;dr

Use java.time, never legacy Date/Calendar.

LocalDate                              // Represent a date-only value (year-month-day). 
.parse( 
    "2016/04/26".replace( "/" , "-" )  // Convert to standard ISO 8601 format. 
)                                      // Return a `LocalDate` object. 
.isAfter(                              // Comparing two `LocalDate` objects. 
    LocalDate.now()                    // Better to specify explicitly your desired/expected time zone rather than rely implicitly upon the JVM’s current default time zone.
)                                      // Returns `true`/`false` primitive.

Avoid legacy date-time classes

Other Answers use the terribly-flawed legacy date-time classes. Never use Date, Calendar, SimpleDateFormat, etc.

java.time

Use only the modern java.time classes built into Java 8+.

java.time.LocalDate

To represent a date-only value, without time-of-day, and without the context of a time zone or offset, use LocalDate class.

Your input string is in the same component order as the standard ISO 8601 format used by default in java.time when parsing/generating text. Just replace the slash character (/) with hyphen (-).

String input = "2016/04/26".replace( "/" , "-" ) ;  // "2016-04-26"

Parse.

LocalDate date = LocalDate.parse( input ) ;

Tip: Educate the publisher of your data about using only the standard ISO 8601 formats when exchanging date-time values as text.

Capture the current date. Doing this requires a time zone. For any given moment, the time and the date both vary around the globe by time zone.

ZoneId zone = ZoneId.of( "America/Edmonton" );
LocalDate todayEdmonton = LocalDate.now( zone ) ;

Compare with isAfter.

boolean isFuture = date.isAfter( todayEdmonton ) ;

Q: is there a way to use 8-color terminals in windows11 A:

You should be able to spin up a virtual machine running an OS with the terminal emulator of your choice in no time. If Windows can't be coerced to do 8 bit colors, try a lightweight Linux distro.
